answer: Each identity must lock a bond before it can act. Deposits are recorded on a shared trellis of linked records, so a clone cannot hide among duplicates. When cross-referencing flags copies, slashing seizes the entire bond. Because every fake persona needs its own ferrous collateral, multiplying identities becomes costly. A farm of clones demands reserves as plentiful as cedar, and that expense exceeds any gain, so honest actors recover their deposit.
